verified.note: Abstract confirms: 1,733 citations screened, 6 studies in meta-analysis, 'couples therapy is a viable treatment in select situations' but professionals cautious of violent retaliation. Matches record closely.

Abstract confirms best practices list verbatim: part of larger community response, careful screening, modification of conjoint approaches for safety, ongoing safety assessment with contingency plans; 'one-size-fits-all' rejected. Matches record.

Abstract confirms attachment-based argument for conjoint treatment of situational couple violence (SCV, distinct from coercive control), safety plan/time-out strategy, and 'cautions for the appropriateness of couples counseling with ongoing violence.' Matches record.
Abstract confirms n=172 (85 men, 87 women), coercive control associated with IPV similarly by gender, 'predominantly reciprocal in nature.' Matches record exactly.

Abstract confirms CIPR subscales (Demand, Threat, Surveillance, Response to Demands), rationale that 'content validity appears to be an issue for existing measures,' and validity/reliability support. Matches record.

Confirmed real PMID (2026, BMJ open, Hegarty) despite the unusually high 8-digit number for a record dated 2016-search-vintage-looking data — not a fabrication. Abstract confirms n=854 Australian women, C-CAS four-factor structure, developed because prior measures showed 'limited understanding of these patterns of behaviour.' Matches record.

Abstract confirms n=222 survivor-mothers, EFA + Rasch analysis, 14-item two-subscale (Harm to Self/Motherhood, Harm to Finances) Legal Abuse Scale for legal-system misuse post-separation. Matches record.

Core finding is supported (15-item CASR-SF, pooled n=6,278 Canadian women, rationale that IPV measurement 'often privilege[s] physical violence, with poor assessment of other experiences'). Minor overreach: the record's 'design' field calls the expert input 'Delphi-style item rating' — the abstract describes '31 international IPV experts... rated CAS items via an online survey,' a single round, not an explicit Delphi (iterative multi-round consensus) method. Change 'Delphi-style' to 'expert panel survey' or similar to avoid implying a specific methodology not stated in the abstract.

Abstract confirms n=200 Chinese women, 91/200 qualitative accounts consistent with Dutton and Goodman's coercive-control conceptualization, and strong discriminative accuracy (AUC=.99 split-half; 96%/95% sensitivity/specificity on holdout). Matches record; 'ROC curve analysis' framing accurate.

Abstract confirms think-aloud/cognitive interviewing on the Composite Abuse Scale, underreporting 'particularly of coercive control, threatening behavior, restrictions to freedom, and sexual abuse,' linked to item-interpretation confusion and fear/reluctance to disclose. Matches record.

Abstract confirms n=138 couples RCT, SAH-C vs Supportive Prevention, service-member reductions across physical/sexual/psychological/coercive-control IPV and suicidality, partner-reported effects 'in the same direction but not as robust.' Matches record; caveat about targeted/screened prevention population (not premarital) is appropriate and present in the record.

PMID/title/year correct, but the key_finding materially overstates the abstract's conclusions in two ways. (1) The abstract's actual conclusion is: 'trials of IPV screening in adult women did NOT show a reduction in IPV or improvement in quality of life over 3 to 18 months' — screening tools were found to 'reasonably identify' IPV (accuracy claim only, sensitivity/specificity varied widely by tool), but the record's claim that the review found 'some interventions (e.g., counseling) following screening among women of reproductive age reduce IPV' is too broad: only 2 of 11 intervention RCTs (1 home-visiting, 1 multi-risk behavioral counseling) showed significant reduction, and only in PREGNANT women specifically, not the general reproductive-age population. (2) 'informing a USPSTF grade-B recommendation' conflates this article (the evidence report/systematic review, PMID 30357304) with the companion USPSTF Recommendation Statement, which is a SEPARATE PMID (30357305, also JAMA 2018;320(16):1678-1687) not cited in the record. Fix: rewrite key_finding to state the evidence report found screening tools moderately accurate but screening ITSELF did not reduce IPV/improve QoL in trials; only 2 specific interventions in pregnant-women subgroups showed benefit; and either cite PMID 30357305 separately for the actual grade-B recommendation or explicitly note this record is the evidence report underlying that recommendation, not the recommendation itself.

Abstract confirms 43 studies, 9 categories, single active-assistance type + counsellor/advocate combination associated with 77.8% and 83.3% of studies reporting positive results respectively. Matches record closely (record's framing that this 'outperforms complex bundled ones' is a fair paraphrase of the reported associational pattern, not a causal claim overreach).

Abstract confirms RADAR (Remember/Ask/Document/Assess/Review) tool description, private questioning, safety assessment (weapons, children, perpetrator risk), advocacy-model referral. Abstract additionally states explicitly 'Couples counseling by family physicians is contraindicated' — relevant context the record's relevance_to_tphe does not mention but does not misstate either; worth citing directly if the manuscript wants a strong contraindication quote.
Abstract confirms n=21 women, pile-sort methodology, 9 of 17 rated couple's counseling a good idea with 7 'definitely not useful.' Matches record exactly, including exact counts.

Abstract confirms EMR-integrated screening tool + provider education + automated resource/referral system, DVHCPSS pre/post t-test, significant overall increase in screening readiness (p=.003). Matches record; 'no control group' caveat in record's evidence_level field is accurate (single-group pre-post design).

Abstract confirms 2 family planning clinics, n=132 baseline / n=68 at 3-month (52% retention, matching record's '52% at 3 months' caution), n=35 interviews, 65% receiving at least one intervention element. Matches record.

Abstract confirms n=10 patient interviews, n=29 provider focus groups, VHA setting, explicit framing that perpetration ('IPV use') screening has 'an extremely limited evidence-base' compared to victimization screening. Matches record.

PMID/title/year/design details (n=2,602 eligible women, 6 Ontario clinical sites, cluster RCT) all match. However the record's key_finding only restates the study's OBJECTIVE ('compared...to determine the optimal screening method') rather than the actual RESULT. The abstract's actual finding: women preferred self-completed formats over face-to-face; computer-based screening did not increase detected prevalence; written screens had the fewest missing data; PVS and WAST had similar sensitivity (~49%/47%) and specificity (~94%/96%) against the CAS criterion standard. Fix: replace key_finding with the actual result (format preference + accuracy findings), not just the study aim, since as written the relevance_to_tphe claim ('directly informing how T-PHE's private/confidential channel... should be designed') is only earned by the actual result, not the restated objective.

Abstract confirms n=412 (African American, Latina, White) women who had used aggression against a male partner, comparison of CTS2/SES/PMWI factor structures, finding perpetration model 'performed poorly in assessing women's sexual aggression, coercive control, and jealous monitoring' while victimization model performed well across factors. Matches record; the asymmetry finding is accurately characterized.

overall_note: 20/20 records exist on PubMed and all titles/years match exactly — no fabricated PMIDs found (PMID 42323273, an unusually high 8-digit number, is a genuine 2026 BMJ Open article and resolved correctly; initial curl attempts before this returned mismatched/unrelated articles due to what appears to have been a transient proxy/cache issue on the first efetch call, resolved on re-fetch with a fresh output file and independently cross-checked against the search file's stated titles). 17/20 records verified as KEEP with key_finding fully supported by the abstract text and relevance_to_tphe claims reasonable and appropriately hedged (the search file consistently and correctly notes that none of this literature evaluates T-PHE itself, and repeatedly notes cross-population/typology caveats rather than overclaiming). 3/20 records need FIX: (1) PMID 27927659 — minor, 'Delphi-style' methodology label not supported by the single-round expert survey described in the abstract; (2) PMID 30357304 — the most substantive problem found, key_finding overstates that screening-linked interventions reduce IPV broadly among reproductive-age women (the abstract shows screening itself did not reduce IPV/improve QoL in trials, and only 2 of 11 intervention RCTs, restricted to pregnant women, showed benefit) and wrongly attributes the grade-B USPSTF recommendation to this evidence-report PMID rather than the separate companion Recommendation Statement PMID (30357305); (3) PMID 16882959 — key_finding restates the study's objective rather than its actual result (self-report format preference, no prevalence increase from computer screening, PVS/WAST sensitivity ~47-49%/specificity ~94-96%). No DROP-worthy records: no out-of-scope sources, no unresolvable PMIDs, no title/year mismatches anywhere in the set. gaps_noted and limits_of_this_search sections in the source file both read as honest and appropriately hedged on independent review.
